admission.justification: The constants-based marking and its rejected text/shape alternatives govern every future decision surface; a new record kind must re-establish its marking.

alternatives.option: Mark records from the writers' own exact constant and skip-step prefixes.
alternatives.reason: Constants move with the writers, so the marking tracks what the product writes; the match is exact/prefix string comparison with no enforced authorship separation — an author typing those exact strings would be muted (unguarded; see L126-MEM-04).

alternatives.option: Match record text patterns on the page.
alternatives.reason: Text matching breaks when writers reword records and risks muting authored decisions.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Record text gains a stable machine prefix owned by the writers.

alternatives.option: Change the stored decision shape to carry a flag.
alternatives.reason: A shape change breaks every reader of the decision log for a marking the projection can carry.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The log schema is versioned with a migration for all readers.

consequences: The newest-five count mutes entries matching the writers' constants, keeping other authored history intact.
context: The newest-five rule must mute product-written records without matching authored text, under the architect time-order ruling.
decider: Architect time-order ruling (Parent a7c93988), carried in the R5 dispositions.

evidence: predicate tests + preview tests + whole-log unsorted test; pytest/vitest green
